transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-24
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Riley Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CSM) -- Oliver Stone (CTO), Priya Nair (VP Eng), Samir Gupta (DevOps), Nina Alvarez (SRE)

Summary: Quick QBR style health check focused on runway (budget vs committed capacity), two recent incidents affecting p95 latency during peak promotions, and negotiation around SLOs/SLA for Dedicated capacity. Decided to accelerate a short pilot with real traffic trace + security review.

Topics: usage trends, cost spikes on promo days, dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs, SLO targets, SOC2 and KMS requirements, pilot scope and timeline.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): ok, hey everyone, thank you for carving out time, this is Maya on the AE side, Riley our se is here too. um Jordan from CSM as well. how's everyone?
[00:14] Oliver (CTO): hey Maya, all good. we wanted to nail down what's actually going to be required to keep the Black Friday-ish promo stable. we saw p95 go sideways last month.
[00:29] Maya: yeah i saw the postmortem notes, can you quickly summarize what you saw? Riley will jump in on the infra side.
[00:34] Oliver: sure. so on Nov 11th we had a 3 hour window where p95 spiked from ~420ms to near 1.8s, error rate ticked up to 1.2%. most of our traffic is inference requests to the hosted endpoint. suspect bursting behavior and tokenization oddities.
[00:50] Riley (SE): um right, from what we saw in the trace you sent, there were a lot of long context chains; KV cache wasn't being hit because each request had unique session tokens. also there was a sudden shift in sequence length distribution, so batching efficiency dropped.
[01:07] Samir (DevOps): just to interject, our system adds a tracking header that might be busting the cache, and we also saw a downstream weight on our side that slowed network egress to the cloud region.
[01:21] Riley: yeah, couple things we can do: prefix caching tweaks, smaller batch caps during the promo to keep latency predictable, and optionally pin to Dedicated capacity for the event so we don't contended with other tenants.
[01:36] Priya (VP Eng): dedicated seems like the safer bet but cost is a real blocker for finance. can you give a delta on committed cost vs hosted for a 1-week promo?
[01:47] Maya: absolutely. we can send committed-sizing scenarios. rough rule of thumb: Dedicated floor reduces p95 variance and gives predictable throughput. for a 1-week promo the per-hour burn may be higher if reserved but the chance of revenue loss is lower. we'll put exact numbers in a spreadsheet.
[02:06] Nina (SRE): also from compliance: we need to confirm SOC2 status of Redwood Private if we move data residency; plus SSO, SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration for keys. we have an internal policy that requires CMEK for stripe/tokenized data.
[02:21] Jordan (CSM): we have a compliance pack, i'll share the SOC2 + security whitepaper, and riley can walk through KMS integrations.
[02:31] Riley: quick note, our Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and HSM in VPC mode; in Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS for envelope encryption, but if you need on-prem HSM that's a Private install.
[02:45] Oliver: ok good, sounds like we need both the security docs and a short pilot to prove the p95 target. what's realistic for SLOs? we were thinking 250ms p95 for simple completion calls.
[02:58] Riley: 250ms p95 for completion at your token lengths and throughput might be aggressive on current gen small models when concurrency is high. we need your traffic trace to simulate. with Dedicated and prefix caching optimized, hitting ~300ms p95 is reasonable; 250ms might require quantization and lower latency models or colocating inference in a closer region.
[03:20] Priya: hmm, so tradeoffs are model quality vs latency and cost. we can consider trimmed prompts for promos. but we need an objective baseline.
[03:29] Maya: ok timeline-wise, proposal: you share a 2-week sample traffic trace; Riley will run bench with our default and a tuned config; we will present three scenarios: Hosted burst (savings), Dedicated (predictable), Private (compliance-heavy) with numbers.
[03:44] Samir: yes we'll extract the traces and scrub PHI, PII. also our security team will want a redacted flow showing headers.
[03:52] Maya: great.

-- mid-call technical deep dive --
[10:12] Riley: going into technical stuff: we saw token seq lengths median 120, 95th ~540. that tail spikes batching. our runtime has options: dynamic batching, per-tenant batch caps, and KV caching. however the cache hit rate depends on prompt reuse; in your case reuse was low during promos.
[10:30] Priya: is there any low-friction change on our side? smaller prompts? removing certain debug headers?
[10:37] Riley: yes, short term: reduce redundant tracking headers, standardize prompt templates, and add a short prefix cache key so sessions with common templates can hit the cache. medium term: add client-side batching or edge cache.
[10:48] Samir: client-side batching would be tricky given our frontend architecture, but we can do a light change in the ingestion lambda.

[17:05] Maya: circling back to costs — we had an example last quarter where a customer saved 18% switching to Dedicated for hotspots. but again, depends on utilization. for you i recommend a 2-week pilot with a small Dedicated pool and auto-burst to Hosted as fallback. that gives a safety net.
[17:22] Oliver: auto-burst sounds attractive. is fallback automatic or do we need to manage routing?
[17:28] Riley: it's policy-driven; Redwood will route requests based on latency SLOs, and there is an explicit fallback plan. note though fallbacks can change tokenization characteristics if you switch model variants.
[17:42] Priya: we also want clear billing visibility: token-level cost, per-route metrics. can we get a per-route dashboard for the pilot?
[17:50] Jordan: yes the Console has per-route breakdowns and cost attribution, we'll give you a demo link.

[24:00] Nina: on security, our checklist: SOC2 attestation, SSO via SAML/Okta, per-request audit logs shipped to our SIEM, and KMS integration. are any of those blockers?
[24:12] Riley: all supported; for audit logs we can stream via TLS to your logging endpoint, or you can pull via API. for KMS we support cloud KMS and bring-your-own keys in Private.
[24:25] Oliver: what's the lead time for Private on-prem deployment? our security team says Private is preferred but it might be long.
[24:33] Maya: Private lead time is typically 6-8 weeks with our on-prem team and integration windows; Dedicated can be provisioned in 48-72 hours for standard regions.
[24:44] Priya: 6-8 weeks is a lot, but ok for long-term. we should scope the pilot on Dedicated then, and if it meets compliance we can talk Private for next quarter.

[31:10] Riley: for the pilot we'll do three benchmark runs: baseline (current config), tuned (prefix cache + batch caps), and dedicated pool run with your trace. i'll attach raw p50/p95 and per-token cost metrics.
[31:24] Samir: do you need sample VPC peering info for network performance tests?
[31:29] Riley: yes that'll help. also if you have egress constraints call them out — we saw your note about limited egress to non-approved regions.

[37:05] Priya: finance will want an explicit SLA for promo windows. can we get a short SLA addendum for dedicated reserved pools with credits for downtime beyond X?
[37:16] Maya: yes we can provide an SLA addendum for Dedicated tiers. standard is 99.9% with credits, but we can discuss tailored terms based on committed spend. Jordan will run point on that.
[37:29] Jordan (CSM): i'll prepare a PCM (pilot commitment memo) with SLA language and run it past legal.

[42:00] Oliver: ok recap — we'll send trace, you'll run bench, send pricing / scenarios, security docs. then pilot kickoff week of Dec 5th.
[42:11] Maya: exactly. additional ask: if you can provide two peak-day windows, that helps us size the Dedicated pool.
[42:20] Samir: we'll supply those.

[45:02] Maya: any other open risks?
[45:06] Nina: just the KMS requirement, need to confirm HSM compat later if Private is chosen.
[45:12] Riley: noted. also, watch out for tokenization differences between model families—when we fallback to a lower-latency variant the cost and quality may differ. we'll add that to the risk register.
[45:26] Maya: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and pricing.
[45:31] Oliver: thanks, appreciate it.
